history.dynasty: Chola (foundation); later patronage by the Hoysalas and the Vijayanagara Empire
history.period: 10th century CE (Chola period; earliest inscriptions 10th c.)
history.summary: The Chokkanathaswamy Temple at Domlur (called Tombalur/Tommalur or Desimanikkapattanam in inscriptions) is considered Bengaluru's oldest temple, built by Rajaraja Chola I after his conquest of Yelahanka Nadu around 1004 CE. The sanctum and two ardhamantapas are of Chola origin (9th-13th c.); the navaranga mantapa with its pillars is a Vijayanagara-era addition. The presiding Vishnu idol with Sridevi and Bhoodevi is carved from saligrama stone brought from the Gandaki river in Nepal. Tamil inscriptions record a 1270 CE donation of door posts by Alagiyar and a 1290 CE grant by Poysala (Hoysala) Vira Ramananda; Devaraya II of Vijayanagara made land and revenue grants to the temple. Repeated modern renovations have left only the sanctum and ardhamantapas with antiquity. Note: one source claims the original deity was Shiva and the Vishnu shrine was added later for the local Vaishnava residents - this is an account of a single source (UNVERIFIED). The temple is also known for its 'pranic energy points' marked inside the complex.

name: Chokkanathaswamy Temple
town_description: Domlur, in eastern Bengaluru, is one of the city's oldest continuously inhabited neighbourhoods, appearing in 10th-century Chola inscriptions as Tombalur or Desimanikkapattanam ('place of indigenous pearls'). Though now a dense urban locality near Indiranagar and Koramangala, it retains the Chokkanathaswamy Temple as the core of its ancient settlement.
